why: Today's CI adds nine shared test-job groups and one shared control-job group while retaining the existing global scheduled workflow queue. The static guard keeps full and changed legs inside the same fixed slots without changing test selection, depth, matrix names, timeouts, permissions, fail-fast or reporting.
note: The final scheduled linter suite passed 232 tests at seed 119120. Removing SC19 made all 52 new controls fail; source restoration matched its original SHA256. Valid controls cover slot permutations, JSON key order, numeric and text slot values and case-insensitive group names. A parsed YAML comparison confirmed that removing the five added job-concurrency maps reproduces the original workflow exactly. Format, lint 18 of 18, ratchet and diff checks passed. One whole pinned typecheck passed all 30 projects in 15.62 seconds, with direct and Python-nested Node 26.13.0 and native pnpm 12.16.1. The first compiler found one Schema.Number diagnostic; Schema.Finite fixed it without suppression. Sibling SIGKILLs followed that failed project, not memory exhaustion. Final HEAD, source, index and shared-lock inode stayed unchanged. No CI dispatch, cancellation, protected local law, platform enforcement or speed claim. Usage and list spend were not exposed; no zero-cost claim.
